record_type_quote: Similar measures of reading performance, the same measures of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity, and similar selection criteria were used in the two studies.

targets.authors: Wadsworth, S. J., DeFries, J. C., Willcutt, E. G., Pennington, B. F., & Olson, R. K.
targets.title: The Colorado Longitudinal Twin Study of Reading Difficulties and ADHD: Etiologies of comorbidity and stability.
targets.evidence_quote: Because of recent concerns about the replication of published results in the behavioral and biomedical sciences (Ioannidis, PLoS Medicine, Vol. 2, 2005, p. e124; Open Science Collaboration, Science, Vol. 349, 2015, p. 943; Pashler & Wagenmakers, Perspectives on Psychological Science, Vol. 7, 2012, pp. 528–530), we have conducted a replication of our recently published analyses of longitudinal reading performance and attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder data from twin pairs selected for reading difficulties (Wadsworth et al., Twin Research and Human Genetics, Vol. 18, 2015, pp. 755–761).
targets.outcome_quote: In general, the patterns of results obtained from these two independent studies were highly similar. Thus, these results clearly illustrate the principle that findings from studies in quantitative behavioral genetics often replicate (Plomin et al., Perspectives on Psychological Science, Vol. 11, 2016, pp. 3–23).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors give an overall positive verdict; smaller estimates and overlapping confidence intervals are not framed as failures.

reasoning: Independent ILTS twin sample retests the 2015 CLDRC findings. Identity and author list match; complete five-page article includes references.
